words.lemma: menmae/menma n-stem, gen. sg. (< *men-men-, = Ved. mánman-)

cognate: heart word *ḱerd- in all (OIr cride, Ved. hṛd-/hṛdaya-, OAv. zərəd-, ON hiarta); mind word from *men- in Irish (menma < *men-men-, formally = Ved. mánman-), Vedic (mánas-, matí-) and Avestan (manah-)
drift_or_renewal: Irish uses the -men- derivative menma where Indo-Iranian has the s-stem *ménos (mánas-, manah-); Old Norse renews the mind term (hugr ok hiarta); Greek likewise has κραδίη καὶ θυμός (renewal, not checked by locus)
shared_syntax: coordinated binomial heart + mind as instrument/source of an inner act: Ved. instr. hr̥dā́ mánasā (often with utá or -ca), OAv. instr. zərədācā manaŋhācā (double -ca); OIr ó + gen. 'from the desire of heart and mind' (other Irish witnesses: ó chride ⁊ ó menmain, glaine cride ⁊ menman)
context: devotion/desire and inner (non-bodily) action: the Irish homily on pilgrimage contrasts leaving one's homeland 'from the desire of heart and mind' with leaving it in body; RV 6.28.5 'I desire Indra with heart and mind', RV 10.119.5 'I bend the thought round with the heart', AVP 1.76 the enemy who assails 'with heart, eye, mind and speech'; Y 31.12 speaking 'with his heart and mind'. Indo-Iranian side is a fixed formula (11 of 91 RV padas with hṛd- also have mánas-, plus OAv. exact match). Irish side: the binomial cride ⁊ menma is frequent (c. 25 hits) but almost wholly in Christian homiletic and translated prose, where Latin corde et mente / in toto corde ... in tota mente (Mt 22:37, itself rendering Greek kardia/dianoia) is an obvious model; 'heart and mind' is also a near-universal pairing. So the Celtic participation could be calque or independent. Note: the slab window of the BC-17317 pivot prints 'cride menman'; the stage-C unit text has 'cride ⁊ menman' (Tironian et dropped in the slab), and the parallel BC-a728a pivot has 'o duthracht cridhi [⁊] o mhenmain' (gen. cride, dat. menmain). AVP 1.17.s4 (hṛdi ... manasā, separate clauses) is a weaker Vedic witness in the same bundle and is not used as an anchor.
phrase: *ḱr̥d- + *men- 'with heart and mind' (Ved. hr̥dā́ mánasā ~ OAv. zərədācā manaŋhācā ~ OIr. cride ⁊ menma)

note: All 169 bundles read (pivots all Middle Irish saints' lives/homilies from CELT, partners mostly late Greek prose). One low-confidence claim: heart+mind binomial (OIr cride ⁊ menma ~ Ved. hṛdā mánasā ~ OAv. zərədācā manaŋhācā), Irish leg likely influenced by Latin corde et mente. Considered and rejected: bláth ⁊ duille ~ θάλλω/φύλλον (biblical flowering-rod motif, generic), ór ⁊ argat, nem ⁊ talam, mother/father pairs (generic).
